minutes.headline: Assessors debated staffing and meeting frequency, then moved to executive session on abatements; the vote count is cut off.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors met remotely, signed expense vouchers and excise batches, and heard a resident ask why his property's valuation rose. A member pressed for more office staff, a written meeting protocol, a vice chair and secretary, and two meetings a month, which another member opposed. A motion to enter executive session on abatements was made and a roll call began, but the result is not in the captions.

public_comment.topic: A resident (Dave) asked whether the board had made an official decision on his property's abatement. He questioned why his valuation rose when the house had not changed, and how estimated taxes are calculated.

The same resident said insurance and refund checks issued in a trust's name cannot be cashed at banks, and that reissuing them is slow. He voiced strong dissatisfaction and mentioned a possible recall.

budget_items.what_was_said: A resident and the board discussed how estimated taxes are projected and a rate figure circulating for the coming year. The board said the rate is not yet produced.
Board members explained that the replacement cost per square foot was raised town-wide for conventional-style homes, raising valuations.
The resident said his assessment rose over the last two years.
Checks are issued in the same name as the bill; banks reject some, and reissue goes through the accountant's office.
The board discussed assessing completion levels on building permits, since this feeds the town's new growth revenue.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors moved to enter executive session on abatements and began a roll call, but the captions do not show the result.
The board told a resident it would take up his abatement request in executive session and that he should hear by the end of the week.
Board members said the replacement cost per square foot was raised town-wide for conventional-style homes, which raised valuations; the resident said his assessment rose over two years.
Kevin Fisher declined the vice chair nomination and Jack accepted the secretary role, treated as agreed with no formal vote in the captions.
Two members are to draft a meeting protocol and send it to legal counsel for review.

why_it_matters: A change in the cost-per-square-foot schedule can raise assessed values on many homes without any change to the houses, so a resident's bill can move on a board's valuation input rather than on anything done to the property.
Abatement requests are decided in closed session, so a resident who applies learns the outcome only afterward, and the board said the tax rate for the coming year has not yet been produced.
watch_next: The board's meeting protocol, once drafted and reviewed by legal counsel, and any decision on how often the board meets.
The tax rate for the coming year, which the board said is not yet produced.
